correctness.rationale: For the root-doubling process after the deterministic first event, the three generator transitions are (s,i,d)->(2s+1,2i-1,d+1) at rate 1, (s+1,i-1,d) at rate (s+i)/2, and (s+1,i+1,d) at rate (s-2-i)/2. Exact generator computations give G(i)=-2, G(i^2)=i^2-6i+s, G(s)=2s, G(d)=1, and G(i z^d)=[2(z-1)i-(z+1)]z^d. With initial (3,1,0), the resulting closed ODE for the mixed transform is solved exactly; differentiation and the second-moment ODE give the covariance and variance. Nonexplosion follows from finitely many root Poisson events and nonexplosive Yule evolution between them; second moments are finite by the quadratic size-generator estimate. A self-contained Python standard-library verifier passed 10,263 exact generator and Taylor checks through order eight. Checks supplement, rather than replace, the infinite analytical proof.

value.rationale: The natural leaf/size imbalance 2L-N removes the first-order degree-frequency effect and exposes a new dimension of fluctuations in a root-doubling growth process. A single exact Poisson-tilted transform simultaneously gives all doubling-count-conditional first moments, sharp negative finite-time covariance -t^2, and an exponentially growing explicit imbalance variance. These facts quantify the effect of global doubling shocks, an observable not treated by the motivating degree-frequency/height work. The invariant is canonical rather than an arbitrarily sliced parameter; a complete conditional law or further asymptotic theory is not necessary for the exact structural finite-time result to be useful.
